meta.executive_summary: The current DIGIT/CMS deployment posture presents severe, systemic risks to sensitive citizen grievance data due to a complete lack of defense-in-depth across the network, container, and application layers. Critical datastores and administrative services are bound directly to 0.0.0.0 without active host firewalls, relying entirely on a single cloud security group as a fragile perimeter. Systemic root causes stem from permissive infrastructure-as-code defaults, unauthenticated service exposures, and dangerous container escape vectors like Docker socket mounts. Priority must be given immediately to restricting network bindings, eliminating default credentials, and enforcing host-level isolation controls.
priority_actions: Enable and configure the host firewall (UFW/iptables) immediately to block direct access to all 33+ published datastore and administrative ports (PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, MinIO, Grafana) currently exposed on 0.0.0.0.
Rotate all default and weak credentials across the deployment configuration and ensure sensitive secrets are managed securely outside of public repository scope.
Remove dangerous container configurations including Docker socket mounts and sensitive host directory volume bindings to prevent container breakout risks.
Patch unauthenticated admin and API surfaces exposed through the nginx reverse proxy and enforce robust authentication and TLS validation controls.

Harden the Ansible deployment pipeline by removing remote scripts piped directly into shells, enabling SSH host-key verification, and binding all container traffic strictly to localhost/internal interfaces.

findings.title: Datastore or admin port published on all interfaces (0.0.0.0)
findings.why: Publishing the PostgreSQL database and Prometheus directly to all interfaces (0.0.0.0) exposes sensitive backend data stores and monitoring metrics to the public internet without authentication.
findings.fix:
Modify docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml to bind ports to localhost only:
```yaml
ports:
  - "127.0.0.1:15432:5432"
```
and similarly for Prometheus:
```yaml
ports:
  - "127.0.0.1:19090:9090"
```

triage.reason: Postgres and Prometheus ports are bound to 0.0.0.0 with no host firewall; reliance solely on cloud security groups.

findings.title: Weak or default credential in deployment config
findings.why: Hardcoded or weak fallback credentials (such as 'eGov@123' or 'admin') are written into the environment files, allowing attackers with file access or default knowledge to easily compromise Keycloak and internal tokens.
findings.fix:
Remove insecure default fallback strings in setup/deployment ansible tasks, requiring credentials to be explicitly defined:
```yaml
TOKEN_EXCHANGE_SYSTEM_PASSWORD={{ kcprep_secrets.json.data.data.token_exchange_system_password }}
```

triage.reason: Default and fallback credentials like egov123 are explicitly configured for administrative and database access.

findings.title: Volume Has Sensitive Host Directory
findings.why: Mounting the entire host Docker container directory or root procfs/sysfs into monitoring containers gives excessive visibility into host internals and other containers, increasing the blast radius if the monitoring container is compromised.
findings.fix: This is expected for log aggregation (Promtail) and metrics collection (Node Exporter) in this specific stack; ensure the mounts are strictly read-only (`:ro`) as currently implemented, or use specialized secure telemetry agents if available. False positive.

triage.reason: Promtail mounts the sensitive host directory /var/lib/docker/containers directly into the container.

findings.title: Docker Socket Mounted In Container
findings.why: Mounting the Docker socket (`/var/run/docker.sock`) inside a container grants root-level control over the Docker daemon, allowing a compromised container to execute arbitrary commands or spin up privileged containers on the host.
findings.fix:
Remove the Docker socket volume mount from the promtail service in docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml:
```yaml
# Remove this line:
# - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
```

triage.reason: Docker socket (/var/run/docker.sock) is mounted inside the promtail container, enabling full host container control.

findings.title: Remote script piped directly into a shell
findings.why: Piping a remote shell script directly into bash executes untrusted code without integrity checking, making the deployment vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks or compromised upstream distribution servers.
findings.fix:
Download the script, verify its checksum, and then execute it in setup/deploy.sh or the Ansible playbook:
```yaml
- name: Download NodeSource setup script
  ansible.builtin.get_url:
    url: https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x
    dest: /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh
    mode: '0700'
- name: Run NodeSource setup script
  ansible.builtin.command: /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh
```

triage.reason: Remote shell script is fetched via curl from nodesource.com and piped directly into bash.

findings.title: Docker image registry used over insecure HTTP
findings.why: Configuring Docker to pull images over insecure registries leaves image pulls vulnerable to interception and malicious tampering via man-in-the-middle attacks.
findings.fix: Ensure `insecure_registries` is explicitly set to an empty list `[]` in group_vars to force TLS usage for all container image fetches.

triage.reason: Docker daemon configuration explicitly includes insecure registry fallback settings.

findings.title: SSH host-key verification disabled
findings.why: Disabling SSH host key checking (`StrictHostKeyChecking=no`) exposes the remote provisioning pipeline to active Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks during initial connection setup.
findings.fix:
Remove or update `ansible_ssh_common_args` in inventory generation scripts to enforce strict checking:
```bash
echo "        ansible_ssh_common_args: '-o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes'"
```

triage.reason: SSH host-key checking is explicitly disabled via StrictHostKeyChecking=no in the deployment generator.

findings.title: Unauthenticated admin/API surface exposed via nginx
findings.why: Exposing the MCP server via an unauthenticated nginx location block permits unauthenticated administrative actions (such as user and tenant creation) from external users.

triage.reason: Unauthenticated admin MCP server endpoints are exposed externally via nginx.

findings.title: Container Capabilities Unrestricted
findings.why: Running containers without capability drops allows processes that break out of the application layer to utilize dangerous Linux capabilities against the host kernel.
findings.fix:
Add capability drops to services in docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml:
```yaml
security_opt:
  - no-new-privileges:true
cap_drop:
  - ALL
```

triage.reason: Containers run with default unrestricted capabilities lacking cap_drop [ALL].

findings.title: Security Opt Not Set
findings.why: Omitting security options like `no-new-privileges` can allow privilege escalation via setuid/setgid binaries inside the running containers.
findings.fix:
Add security options to the service definitions in docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml:
```yaml
security_opt:
  - no-new-privileges:true
```

triage.reason: Missing security_opt (no-new-privileges) on container deployments.

findings.title: Container Traffic Not Bound To Host Interface
findings.why: Binding container ports to all interfaces without specifying an IP address exposes internal service management ports directly to the public internet.
findings.fix:
Explicitly bind ports to localhost in docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml:
```yaml
ports:
  - "127.0.0.1:18091:8091"
```

triage.reason: Container ports are published on all interfaces without binding to 127.0.0.1 or utilizing a host firewall.

findings.title: Healthcheck Not Set
findings.why: Without a healthcheck configured, orchestration tools cannot accurately determine if a service has started successfully or failed silently, complicating automated recovery.
findings.fix: Add an appropriate healthcheck block to migration and dependent services in docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml.

triage.reason: Missing healthchecks are reliability-only concerns rather than direct security controls.

findings.title: Ensure that HTTPS url is used with uri
findings.why: Using plain HTTP instead of HTTPS for internal API calls exposes tokens and secrets in transit if the network path is unencrypted or monitored.
findings.fix: Since OpenBao is running locally on the loopback interface (`127.0.0.1`), plain HTTP is acceptable for local IPC. False positive.

triage.reason: Internal service checks use plain HTTP endpoints for credential or status exchanges.

findings.title: File created without an explicit restrictive mode
findings.why: Creating configuration or state files without explicit restrictive modes can expose sensitive secrets or configurations to unprivileged local system users.
findings.fix:
Add an explicit `mode` parameter to file creation tasks in the Ansible playbook:
```yaml
file:
  path: "{{ digit_dir }}"
  state: directory
  mode: '0700'
```

triage.reason: Files are created in tasks without explicitly enforcing restrictive access modes.

findings.title: Ensure that certificate validation isn't disabled with uri
findings.why: Disabling certificate validation (`validate_certs: false`) leaves API healthchecks and validation tasks vulnerable to interception and spoofing.
findings.fix: Ensure `validate_certs` is only conditionally disabled when testing sandbox environments over plain HTTP, keeping it strictly enabled (`true`) when TLS is active.

triage.reason: Certificate validation relies on conditional flags that may disable TLS verification.

findings.title: Privileged Ports Mapped In Container
findings.why: Mapping privileged ports (< 1024) inside containers is unnecessary and increases attack surfaces if services run as root inside the container.
findings.fix: Map container ports to unprivileged high-numbered ports on the host as currently implemented (`18080:80`). False positive.

triage.reason: Mapping privileged port 80 to a high host port is a benign equivalent-security rewrite.

findings.title: Shell pipeline without pipefail (failures go undetected)
findings.why: Shell pipelines that do not enforce `set -o pipefail` can mask failures in early commands of a pipe, leading Ansible to consider a failing command successful.
findings.fix:
Prepend `set -euo pipefail;` to shell command blocks in Ansible tasks:
```yaml
ansible.builtin.shell: |
  set -euo pipefail
  docker ps -a ... | grep ...
```

triage.reason: Ansible shell commands execute pipelines without strict pipefail error checking.

findings.title: Host Namespace is Shared
findings.why: Sharing host namespaces (`pid: host`) allows processes inside the container to view and potentially interact with all processes running on the host OS.
findings.fix: This configuration is required for node-exporter to correctly scrape host performance metrics. Ensure it is appropriately isolated and protected. False positive.

triage.reason: Host PID namespace sharing via read-only mounts is required and legitimate for monitoring agents.

findings.title: Memory Not Limited
findings.why: Unbounded memory usage allows a single runaway container or denial-of-service condition to exhaust all memory on the host, crashing other critical services.
findings.fix:
Add resource constraints under the service definition in docker-compose.yaml:
```yaml
deploy:
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 512M
```

triage.reason: Missing resource limits are reliability controls, acceptable for isolated deployments.

findings.title: systemd service runs without hardening (NoNewPrivileges=true)
findings.why: Systemd services running without hardening parameters like `NoNewPrivileges=true` can be exploited for privilege escalation if the application binary is compromised.
findings.fix:
Add hardening directives under the `[Service]` block of the systemd unit template:
```ini
[Service]
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=full
ProtectHome=true
```

triage.reason: Systemd service files lack hardening options such as NoNewPrivileges=true.

findings.why: Systemd services running without hardening parameters like `NoNewPrivileges=true` can be exploited for privilege escalation if the application binary is compromised.
findings.fix:

findings.why: Systemd services running without hardening parameters like `NoNewPrivileges=true` can be exploited for privilege escalation if the application binary is compromised.

triage.reason: Systemd service files lack hardening options such as NoNewPrivileges=true.

findings.title: nginx is missing the security header: server_tokens off
findings.why: Leaving nginx server tokens enabled leaks exact software versions in HTTP headers, aiding attackers in targeting known vulnerabilities.
findings.fix: Add `server_tokens off;` inside the `http` or `server` block of the nginx configuration template.

triage.reason: Nginx configuration lacks server_tokens off to prevent version disclosure.

findings.title: nginx is missing the security header: Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)
findings.why: Leaving nginx server tokens enabled leaks exact software versions in HTTP headers, aiding attackers in targeting known vulnerabilities.
findings.fix: Add `server_tokens off;` inside the `http` or `server` block of the nginx configuration template.

triage.reason: Nginx configuration lacks server_tokens off to prevent version disclosure.

findings.title: nginx is missing the security header: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
findings.why: Leaving nginx server tokens enabled leaks exact software versions in HTTP headers, aiding attackers in targeting known vulnerabilities.
findings.fix: Add `server_tokens off;` inside the `http` or `server` block of the nginx configuration template.

triage.reason: Nginx configuration lacks server_tokens off to prevent version disclosure.

findings.title: Security lint rule disabled in .ansible-lint
findings.why: Disabling key security lint rules in `.ansible-lint` can allow security regressions and dangerous coding patterns to pass unnoticed into production deployment scripts.
findings.fix: Remove security-related rule exclusions from the `.ansible-lint` configuration file to enforce robust static analysis.

triage.reason: Disabling specific linter rules is an acceptable repository maintenance configuration.

findings.title: Shared Volumes Between Containers
findings.why: Sharing volumes across multiple containers can create unintended data coupling or race conditions if multiple services write to the same location.
findings.fix: Ensure shared volumes like Java agents are mounted strictly read-only (`:ro`) as implemented (`./otel/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar:/otel/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar:ro`). False positive.

triage.reason: Shared read-only volumes for instrumentation agents (otel agent jar) are required and safe.

findings.title: Cpus Not Limited
findings.why: Not limiting CPU utilization can let a single container monopolize CPU cores during high traffic or processing spikes, starving other components.
findings.fix:
Add CPU limits under the deploy section in docker-compose:
```yaml
deploy:
  resources:
    limits:
      cpus: '0.5'
```

triage.reason: Unrestricted CPU limits are reliability controls rather than direct security vulnerabilities.
